artifact_render_contract.purpose: Provide a stable view contract for external render surfaces so they do not have to infer layout from prose or depend on runtime JavaScript or Mermaid for critical meaning.

planned.label: Current focus or next planned step

hard_rules: Critical meaning must render correctly with HTML and CSS alone.
JavaScript may enhance interaction but must not be required to show milestone rows, current focus, candidate next consumers, or deferred scope.
Mermaid is optional enhancement only and must never be the sole carrier of state meaning.
If the live artifact cannot read refreshed files at view time, the scheduled refresh must rewrite the artifact itself from current manifest data.
Do not present candidate next consumers as the current active implementation lane.
When next_required_decision.state=settled, do not invent a planned or open next lane in the artifact.
Render every deferred item with item-level activation criteria for candidate-next and current-focus promotion; do not collapse the deferred list into unlabeled gray boxes only.
Do not promote a deferred item into candidate-next or current-focus unless the manifest-declared activation conditions are actually satisfied by live repo truth.

Route/UI widening, runtime DB writes, and schema widening must remain separately controlled unless the same freeze admits them explicitly.

items.title: Runtime DB writes
items.current_boundary: Current `main` treats review/document-trace runtime DBs as read-only evidence-plane surfaces. Runtime DB safety rails, operator authority labeling, and browser proof are landed, but write-enabled runtime behavior remains explicitly out.
candidate_next_requires: Live repo truth must prove that the read-only evidence-plane model is insufficient and that the required writes belong in runtime snapshots rather than the control-plane DB.
A new freeze must explicitly admit write-enabled runtime behavior and define which runtime DBs may be written, by which surfaces, and under what isolation model.
The lane must define operator-safe authority rules that prevent accidental writes or migrations against immutable runtime snapshots.
current_focus_requires: A planned or open lane must name the exact services, scripts, routes, and write paths that will perform runtime writes.
The proof plan must use isolated runtime state and preserve the hard rule that validate-only actions remain validate-only and must not seed or generate artifacts.
Docs and operator surfaces must identify write authority, rollback expectations, and cleanup semantics before the lane can become current focus.

items.title: Schema widening
items.current_boundary: Multiple freezes in the bounded chain explicitly keep schema widening out. Current `main` lands additive consumers and operator surfaces without changing the bounded packet's schema boundary.
candidate_next_requires: A concrete blocker must prove that the required consumer, validation surface, or operator flow cannot be supported within the existing schema.
A new freeze must enumerate the exact tables, models, fields, or indexes that would widen and the exact consumers that require them.
The lane must keep schema widening separate from route/UI or runtime-write widening unless the same freeze explicitly admits a combined tranche.
current_focus_requires: A planned or open write-enabled lane must name the exact model files, migration files, services, tests, and verification steps that own the schema change.
The proof plan must include migration execution and direct validation of the widened schema boundary rather than only prose justification.
The active packet and front-door docs must update together because schema widening changes the meaning of the bounded lane, not just its implementation detail.

items.title: Route/UI widening
items.current_boundary: Current `main` already ships the bounded review, document-trace, workbench-compare, and Candidate B Trace posture plus runtime-authority transparency. The settled Layer3/APS packet still explicitly keeps broader route or UI widening out.
candidate_next_requires: Browser/operator evidence must prove that the shipped route/UI posture is insufficient, ambiguous, or incomplete for the intended operator task.
A new freeze must specify the exact page, route, API, and navigation surfaces that would widen, and must distinguish additive new surfaces from edits to shipped review/document-trace/workbench pages.
The lane must preserve current runtime-authority and validate-only boundaries unless a separate freeze reopens them.
current_focus_requires: A planned or open lane must name the exact frontend and backend owner files plus the headed/headless Chrome validation flow that will prove the widened surface.
The lane must update the active front-door docs in step with the implementation so operator guidance does not drift behind the shipped UI.
Runtime DB writes and schema widening must remain separately admitted; route/UI widening alone is not permission to reopen them.
